title: Coastal-Style Chicken Stew
description: This is a kidney-friendly recipe for coastal-style chicken stew. It features chicken thighs, red bell pepper, celery and eggplant seasoned with oregano and garlic.
steps: Place 1/2 liter of water in a skillet.
Remove skin from chicken leg quarters and add them to the skillet.
Crush garlic. Finely chop all remaining ingredients and add them to the chicken.
Cook over low heat for 30 minutes.
Serve chicken with the stew sauce that has formed.
hints: Substitute chicken breast for chicken thighs if desired.

title: Tortilla Pinwheels
description: Throw a party with Tortilla Pinwheels for people on a dialysis diet. Your mouth will water with this kidney-friendly recipe.
ingredients: 3 ounces cooked unprocessed turkey breast, cut into small cubes
steps: Spread cream cheese over each tortilla to cover. Sprinkle with dried cilantro.
Place remaining ingredients in a bowl and mix.
Divide mixed ingredients into 2 portions. Place half on each tortilla and roll up tightly.
Trim ends and cut each roll into 6 pieces.
hints: Wrap the uncut roll in plastic wrap and refrigerate until ready to slice and serve.
Compare tortilla brands and select the one lowest in sodium.

title: Colombian-Style Samosas
description: These kidney-friendly triangles from India are a tasty option for your next meal.
ingredients: 6 sheets puff pastry or phyllo dough
steps: Chop beef and onions and fry with the tablespoon of oil and thyme until browned.
Remove from heat and add curry powder and pepper.
Take a sheet of pastry and form a triangular cone by folding the edges around itself, sealing with beaten egg and leaving one side open for filling.
Fill with beef mixture and seal.
Heat oil and fry samosas until golden brown.
To make the cilantro sauce, finely chop cilantro and walnuts. Mix with chili powder, garlic powder and lemon juice in a small bowl.
Serve hot with cilantro sauce.
hints: Samosas are triangle-shaped turnovers, a traditional food of India.

title: Country Salad
description: DaVita dietitian Jennie has patients who love her easy egg salad recipe, and you’re sure to love it too. Try it in a sandwich, on a salad or on low-sodium crackers for a high-quality protein snack.
steps: Wash lettuce leaves. Drain and cut into small pieces.
Bring 2 cups of water to a boil in a pot. When it boils, remove the pot from the burner and add the juice of half a lemon, then add the onion and let it sit for 10 minutes. After the 10
minutes, remove onion, let cool and cut into half-moons.
Cut carrot into julienne strips.
In a skillet, sauté corn kernels until golden and tender. Let cool.
In a cup, mix 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 1-1/2 tablespoons lemon juice and pepper to make the vinaigrette.
In a bowl, combine all ingredients, including the corn and the vinaigrette, and toss.
Serve immediately.
hints: You can use vinegar instead of lemon to mellow the onion and for the vinaigrette.
Adding the vinaigrette is optional.

title: Lettuce and Mango Salad
description: Start every meal with a Lettuce and Mango Salad, a combination of lettuce, mango and yogurt.
steps: Wash lettuce and cut into thin strips.
Peel mango and cut into small cubes.
In a separate bowl, mix unsweetened yogurt with sweetener and lemon juice.
Add mango and lettuce to the yogurt mixture.
Toss.
hints: You can replace the mango with another low-potassium fruit of your choice.

title: Chicken and Rice Soup
description: This hearty soup can warm you up on any cold day. Potatoes are high-potassium vegetables, but the recommended portion makes this a kidney-friendly dish.
steps: Wash potatoes well, peel and cut. Place in a pan, cover completely with water and bring to a boil. Drain and repeat the process.
Peel and cut carrots. Chop garlic and onion.
Remove bones and skin from chicken and rinse well.
Place all ingredients except rice and cilantro in a pot with the water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 45 minutes more.
Add rice and continue cooking for 25 minutes more.
Remove chicken from the pot. Cut into small pieces and return to the pot.
Add pepper to taste.
Serve garnished with finely chopped cilantro.
hints: To reduce potassium, soak the peeled, chopped potatoes in a bowl of water, changing the soaking water several times. Then add to the soup without the soaking water.

title: High-Protein Strawberry Smoothie
description: Looking for a fitness-boosting snack or a quick add-on to a meal? It’s also popular with the young, hip and health-conscious crowd. DaVita dietitian Judy from Michigan presents the High-Protein Strawberry Smoothie.
steps: Place strawberries in the blender and blend until smooth.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Add all ingredients and continue blending until smooth.
hints: If using frozen fruit, add 1/4 cup water instead of the 1/2 cup ice. How “frozen” the fruit is determines how full you can fill the blender. It will also give you a “softer” consistency than a smoothie, which is very refreshing on hot days.
Adjust the amount of sugar or low-calorie sweetener to your taste.

title: Tropical Salad
description: Gooseberries, apples and strawberries are the stars of this tropical fruit salad created by DaVita dietitian Josefina from Colombia.
steps: In a skillet over medium heat, combine butter, sugar and two cups of water. Add halved goldenberries and cook until soft and the mixture becomes a light syrup. Let sit for a few minutes.
Separately, cut lettuce into very thin strips and cut unpeeled apple into thin wedges. Cut strawberries into medium slices.
Dress the lettuce and fruit mixture with mayonnaise.
Drizzle the salad with the goldenberry syrup.
hints: You can serve this salad with chicken or fish.
If desired, you can replace the refined sugar with a sugar substitute.

title: Festival Salad
description: This combination of flavors will add a new twist to your celebrations.
steps: In a skillet over medium heat, combine butter, sugar and two cups of water. Add halved goldenberries and cook until soft and the mixture becomes a light syrup. Let sit for a few minutes.
Separately, cut lettuce into very thin strips and cut unpeeled apple into thin wedges. Cut strawberries into medium slices.
Dress the lettuce and fruit mixture with mayonnaise.
Drizzle the salad with the goldenberry syrup.
hints: You can serve this salad with chicken or fish.
If desired, you can replace the refined sugar with a sugar substitute.

title: Pumpkin Sorbet
description: This cool, kidney-friendly treat can help on hot summer days.
steps: Wash pumpkin well, peel and cut into small pieces.
Bring water to a boil.
When water is boiling, add pumpkin and cook until slightly softened.
Remove from heat and let cool.
Blend pumpkin, milk and sugar until thick and smooth.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes and serve well chilled.
hints: The milk can be skim or lactose-free.

title: Salsa Verde
description: Tomatillos, cilantro and jalapeño pepper combine with onion, garlic and lime juice to make this low-sodium Salsa Verde.
steps: Soak tomatillos in a medium bowl of water for 5 minutes. Place a small plate on top of the tomatillos to keep them submerged. While tomatillos soak, line a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil and preheat the broiler with a rack 4 inches below the heat source.
Remove husks and stems from soaked tomatillos. Rinse off any sticky residue left on the skin. Pat tomatillos dry and cut in half.
Remove stem from jalapeño and cut into quarters. Cut onion into quarters.

Place tomatillos and jalapeño cut-side down on the prepared baking sheet. Place garlic clove and onion quarters on the baking sheet. Broil for 5 to 7 minutes until small charred or lightly browned spots appear. Adjust the time as needed and watch carefully, since they can burn quickly. Remove from oven.
Carefully transfer the broiled vegetables and their juices to a food processor or blender. Add cilantro, lime juice, salt and black pepper.
Pulse until smooth with no large chunks of tomatillo. Be careful not to turn it into a purée. The salsa will be thin, but it will thicken after it has been refrigerated for a few hours.
hints: Remove the seeds and ribs from the jalapeño for a mild salsa, or add another jalapeño for more heat.
Look for firm tomatillos.
Salsa Verde can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to one week, or in the freezer for future use.
Soaking tomatillos helps remove the sticky residue from the skin.
Serve warm or cold over eggs, tacos or your favorite Mexican dish.

title: Lemon Blueberry Bread
description: Try Lemon Blueberry Bread the next time you feel like baking something sweet and kidney-friendly with a little zing.
ingredients: Flour for dusting the loaf pan
2 tablespoons lemon extract, 4 large egg whites
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Coat a 9” x 5” x 3” loaf pan with cooking spray and dust with flour.
In a large bowl, combine flour and baking powder.
In another bowl, mix oil, 2/3 cup sugar, extract and egg whites.
Add the oil mixture to the flour mixture, alternating with milk. Beat just until mixed; do not overbeat.
Fold in blueberries and lemon zest.
Pour batter into loaf pan and bake for 40-50 minutes or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Prepare the glaze while the bread is baking. In a small saucepan, combine sugar and lemon juice. Heat until sugar dissolves.
Once you remove the bread from the oven, poke holes in the top at 1” intervals and pour the lemon glaze over the bread.
hints: People with diabetes can make one or more of the following changes:
Omit the lemon glaze and reduce the portion to 1/2 slice.
Substitute Splenda® sugar substitute for the sugar. Nutrition content changes to 154 calories and 17 grams carbohydrate per slice; other nutrients stay the same.
Counts as 1/2 starch, 1/2 fruit, low potassium, 1 fat and 1 carbohydrate choice.

title: Mediterranean Pasta
description: Mediterranean Pasta is a simple, kidney-friendly pasta dish for two. Pour homemade vinaigrette over the pasta and add a small amount of tomato and cheese.
steps: Peel cherry tomatoes and cut into slices.
Grate cheese.
Finely chop onion and cilantro.
Mix cold cooked pasta with tomato, cheese, onion and cilantro.
Combine vinegar, olive oil, water and pepper and pour over pasta.
Heat over low heat for 3 minutes and serve hot.
hints: Use whole wheat pasta for more fiber.

title: Peach and Blueberry Crisp
description: Peach and Blueberry Crisp is kidney-friendly and packed with antioxidants, with tasty warm, tender peaches under a sweet crumb topping.
ingredients: 7 fresh peaches or 4 cups canned peach slices, drained
steps: Remove pits and cut peaches into 3/4″ slices.
Spray a 12″ x 12″ baking pan with cooking spray. Place peaches and blueberries in the pan.
Sprinkle sugar and lemon juice over the fruit.
In a bowl, mix flour and brown sugar. Use two knives to cut the butter into the flour and sugar mixture until crumbly. Sprinkle the
crumbs over the fruit.
Bake at 375° F for 45 minutes or longer, until fruit is tender and crumbs are golden brown.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
hints: Substitute 4 cups drained canned peach slices when fresh peaches are out of season.

title: Chicken Macaroni Bake
description: Chicken Macaroni Bake is an easy-to-make, kidney-friendly one-dish meal.
steps: Cook macaroni in three cups of hot water with one teaspoon oil for 20 minutes. Once cooked, drain, rinse with room-temperature water and set aside.
Cook chicken breast in a cup of water with the two chopped garlic cloves, the red onion cut into large pieces and the cumin. Once the chicken is cooked, let it cool and shred it.
Finely dice the white onion (brunoise) and sauté in a skillet with the 3 tablespoons margarine and one teaspoon sunflower oil. Then add to the macaroni along with the chicken.
Beat eggs with the cup of milk and add to the mixture. Stir ingredients very well and pour into a greased and floured pan to keep it from sticking.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180° C for 25 minutes or until golden.
hints: Turkey can be substituted for chicken in this recipe.

title: Mixed Vegetable Salad
description: Mixed Vegetable Salad consists of lettuce combined with cauliflower, cucumber, radish and onion, then seasoned with a splash of vinegar. Try it for a refreshing lunch or dinner salad.
steps: Wash all vegetables.
Place water in a pan, bring to a boil and cook cauliflower.
Cut lettuce into strips.
Slice cucumber.
Thinly slice radishes. Slice onion.
Mix all vegetables and add vinegar to taste.
hints: To enhance the flavor, you can add lemon juice or fruit vinegar.

title: Mojo Sauce
description: Jalapeño pepper, citrus juice, cilantro, cumin and oregano combine with olive oil to make this popular Cuban Mojo sauce. Try it with eggs or meat dishes.
steps: Remove seeds from jalapeño pepper.
Place ingredients in a blender or food processor and blend until smooth.
Store sauce in a covered container in the refrigerator for up to one week.
hints: Substitute parsley for cilantro if you prefer. Replace the jalapeño with the chile pepper of your choice.
Adjust cumin and oregano to taste.
Use Mojo Sauce as a marinade or sauce. Try it with Sylvia’s Cuban-Style Rice recipe.

title: Potato and Egg Salad in Curry Sauce
description: This lower-sodium egg salad has a unique combination of flavors. Try it at your next meal.
steps: Boil eggs for 10 minutes.
Peel potatoes and boil them.
When both are done, remove and let cool.
Peel eggs and cut potatoes in half.
Chop onion, green onion and garlic. Brown them in a skillet with oil and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove from heat as soon as they are golden and place in a food processor with milk and curry powder. Process until smooth.
Place curry sauce in a saucepan and dissolve cornstarch in it.
Bring to heat and cook, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, until thickened, then remove from heat.
Cut eggs in half, combine with potatoes and top with curry sauce.
Garnish with finely chopped fresh herbs. Serve immediately.
hints: If desired, first place 2 egg halves and half a potato on each plate and then top each one with curry sauce.
To reduce potassium, first cut the potatoes and soak them in 2 cups of water for 2 – 4 hours. Then place them on a clean kitchen towel to remove excess water before cooking.

title: Rice Primavera
description: Rice Primavera is an easy side dish to add to any meal.
steps: Cut bell pepper into julienne strips.
Finely chop onion.
Sauté onion and bell pepper in a little oil until onion is soft.
Add rice, let it turn translucent, then add water and peas.
Cover and cook until rice is tender.
hints: Refrigerate leftovers for a quick meal later.

title: Rice with Pumpkin
description: Rice with Pumpkin is a special rice dish made with pumpkin, red onion and garlic for extra flavor and nutrients.
steps: Peel pumpkin, wash it and cut into small cubes or grate on the coarse side of a grater.
Chop onion and garlic.
Heat oil in a medium skillet or pot and sauté the vegetables.
Rinse rice.
Add rice to the vegetables, sauté for a few minutes and add water.
Boil until the water is absorbed.
Stir the rice, cover and lower the heat so it cooks slowly until tender, about 15 minutes.
Let rest and serve.
hints: Use brown rice for more fiber and flavor.

title: Chicken with Eggplant
description: Add some flavor to your kidney diet with Monica’s delicious chicken and apple curry. Monica, a DaVita renal dietitian from Minnesota, creates a kidney-friendly curry dish by replacing cow’s milk with rice milk and using low-sodium chicken broth.
steps: Rinse chicken, remove skin and cook for about 20 minutes.
Wash eggplant and zucchini and, without peeling, cut into pieces about 1 centimeter wide. Set aside.
Peel onion and cut into squares slightly smaller than the eggplant; set aside as well.
Wash bell pepper, cut in half, remove seeds and cut into small squares. Set aside.
Dip ripe tomato in boiling water for a few seconds, peel and finely chop. Set aside.
Peel and crush garlic cloves and set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pot. Add chopped onion. Let it soften without browning too much, stirring occasionally.
Add eggplant to the pot and fry for about 2 minutes over medium heat.
Add bell pepper and let it soften slightly. Stir occasionally with a wooden spoon.
Add the precooked chicken.

Add zucchini and crushed garlic and cook 1 or 2 minutes over low heat, then immediately add chopped tomato and stir again. Add pepper and let everything cook over low heat for about 15 minutes or until vegetables are cooked.
hints: Don’t add the eggplant and zucchini too soon, or they will lose their texture and flavor.
To reduce the potassium in this recipe, you can dice the eggplant and zucchini, then soak them in warm water for 2 to 4 hours. Discard the water and continue with the recipe.

title: Beef and Lentil Burgers
description: Lentils, egg whites and ground beef are the three protein sources in these Beef and Lentil Burgers. The lentils add a fiber boost of 2.6 grams.
steps: Soak lentils in water for 6 hours before making the burgers, changing the water every 2 hours.
Crush garlic and chop onion and bell pepper.
Grind or mash lentils into a dough, adding garlic, onion and bell pepper.
Knead well, add the three egg whites, ground beef and 2 tablespoons wheat flour and continue kneading.
Heat oil in a skillet while shaping the burgers by hand.
Fry burgers on both sides until golden brown, watching that they don’t burn.
hints: Instead of flour, you can add bread crumbs, and you can add cilantro or parsley (15 grams) to taste.
You can also use other legumes, such as green peas or beans, as you prefer. You can make meatballs with the same mixture.
You can also use other legumes, such as green peas or beans, as you prefer.

title: Cuban-Style Rice
description: Rice seasoned with cilantro, cumin and oregano, plus golden plantains served with eggs, are the ingredients in this tasty, lower-potassium version of Cuban-Style Rice.
serving_size: 2/3 cup rice mixture, 3 plantain pieces, 2 eggs
steps: Prepare rice in a rice cooker or according to package directions. Add bay leaf and water before cooking. Chop onion and tomato. Peel and then cut the
plantain diagonally into 12 pieces. Chop cilantro and garlic. Cut lime into quarters.
Combine dried oregano, cumin and salt in a very small bowl. Set aside.
In a 2-quart skillet over medium heat, sauté onion and garlic in 1/2 tablespoon olive oil. Once garlic and onion are fragrant, add tomato and cook for a few minutes.
Add steamed rice and cilantro and stir. Sprinkle dry seasonings over the top and stir until all ingredients are combined; set aside.
In a skillet, heat 1/2 tablespoon olive oil, add plantains and cook for 2 minutes, turn and cook until golden brown.
In a separate skillet, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat, crack eggs into the pan and cook to desired doneness.
On a plate, place 1/2 cup rice and 3 plantain pieces. Top each serving with 2 eggs.
Squeeze the juice of a lime wedge over each plate.
hints: The plantain portion is small because plantains are high in potassium. If you are not on a low-potassium diet, plantains can be increased to 2 medium or 1 large plantain.
When cooking rice, use a 1:2 ratio: 1 cup rice to 2 cups water.
If you don’t have lemon or lime, try sprinkling 1/4 teaspoon vinegar on each serving for extra flavor.

title: Andean Soup
description: Make this kidney-friendly Andean soup recipe, and your whole family is sure to ask for seconds!
steps: Finely chop onions and cilantro. Crush garlic.
Cut cheese into small pieces.
Peel potatoes and cut into cubes. Cover potatoes completely with water and bring to a boil. Drain and repeat the process. Set potatoes aside.
Bring broth to a boil with onions and garlic.
Stir in potatoes, milk and cheese.
When cheese has melted, add cilantro.
After turning off the heat, add 4 eggs to the soup one at a time, taking care not to break the yolks.
hints: Look for low-potassium chicken broth that does not contain potassium chloride.
Not recommended if phosphorus is not under control.

title: Chicken Pinchos
description: Grilled chicken skewers seasoned with adobo and guava barbecue sauce are sure to please everyone at the table.
ingredients: 1 cup guava BBQ sauce (see recipe on DaVita.com)
steps: Cut chicken thighs into two-inch, bite-size pieces. If using bamboo skewers, soak them in water for 1/2 hour to keep them from burning.
Mix adobo seasoning, oregano, vinegar, olive oil and bay leaves and place in a zip-top bag.
Add chicken to the marinade. Refrigerate for at least half an hour or overnight.
Heat the grill and grease the grates once hot.
Thread chicken onto skewers and place on the hot grill. Brown for 5 minutes on each side.
Baste skewers with guava barbecue sauce or another low-sodium barbecue sauce and cook for about 4 minutes more.
hints: Keep chicken pieces the same size to ensure even cooking.
Find recipes for guava barbecue sauce and other low-sodium barbecue sauces on DaVita.com.

title: Deviled Green Beans
description: Add a touch of flavor to your next meal with this kidney-friendly recipe for Deviled Green Beans. Yellow mustard, black pepper and Worcestershire sauce turn ordinary green beans into a delicious deviled treat.
steps: Prepare green beans according to package directions.
Make a sauce by mixing 2 teaspoons melted margarine, mustard, pepper and Worcestershire sauce. Heat the mixture in the microwave for 30 seconds.
Toss the sauce with the hot green beans.
Mix remaining margarine (melted) with bread crumbs. Sprinkle over green beans and serve.
hints: Fresh or low-sodium canned green beans can be used in place of frozen green beans.

title: Lemon and Thyme Vinaigrette Dressing
description: This low-sodium dressing can add flavor to any salad.
steps: Wash and drain all vegetables that need it.
Combine all ingredients in a salad bowl. Blend all ingredients.
Add dressing to salad to taste.
hints: Herbs such as mint, marjoram or oregano can be used to vary the flavor.

title: Strawberry Shake
description: Strawberries blended with yogurt and a touch of vanilla make the perfect energy boost or add-on to round out a meal.
steps: Blend all ingredients until the mixture is smooth.
Divide into 4 servings and enjoy.
hints: Freeze extra servings for later.

title: Quick Skillet-Glazed Chicken
description: Quick Skillet-Glazed Chicken is full of tasty ingredients like honey, basil and balsamic vinegar, which are also powerful antioxidants. This kidney-friendly recipe is high in lean protein and low in saturated fat.
steps: Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add chicken and sprinkle with pepper.
Sauté chicken for 5 minutes on each side, until browned.
Add balsamic vinegar and sauté for one minute, turning chicken to coat.
Wash and finely chop basil.
Add honey and basil. Stir and turn chicken to coat.
Cook for one minute more.
hints: You can season the chicken with aromatic herbs or your favorite low-sodium seasonings. Garlic and onion go well with black pepper.
If you are on a low-protein diet, reduce the portion to half a chicken breast, or use boneless chicken thighs instead of breasts.

title: Kursan With Lamb and Vegetables
ingredients: A teaspoon of the mix of seven Arab spices
1 large tomato, peeled and chopped (180 g)
1/2 tablespoon of tomato paste, mixed in 475 ml of water
2 small tomatoes (250 g), cut into fried and filtered boxes
Tablespoon of the mixture of seven Arab spices
steps: In a deep frying pan, place the onions in the vegetable oil over a low heat until golden.
Take it out from the heat, add the lamb and stir until it mixes.
When the mutton becomes brown, add spices, salt and crushed garlic.
Add potatoes, tomatoes, and mixed tomato paste; keep the pan on medium heat until the lamb is tender.
When serving, place the bread on a serving plate, then add potatoes and lamb with vegetables over the bread. Garnish with crushed parsley
hints: The seven Arabic spices usually contain black pepper, cumin, cinnamon, cloves, garlic powder and ground black lemon, all crushed and mixed together.

title: Vegetarian Pizza
steps: Mix all ingredients together, minus the toppings, leave for one hour.
Then cut the dough into 3 balls and roll the dough thin.
Chop tomato and green pepper. Spread sauce evenly across dough
1 tablespoon of pizza sauce, then put on tomato, green pepper and mozzarella evenly on each pizza.
Place in the oven for 10 minutes at 180˚C.
hints: Portions: 3 Serving Size: 1 pizza

title: Eggplants roll
steps: Slice the eggplant lengthwise and wash it once.
Put in an oven pan, the dry the eggplant with tissue.
Add some olive oil on each side.
Bake in the oven on 180 for 30 minutes.
In a medium bowl, add the cheese and the spices and mix well, then add the olive oil.
Bring the eggplant and roll it with the cheese mix.
Serve it in a room temperature or cold.

title: Loqaymat
description: Recipe submitted by  Qatif Dietitian
steps: Place the flour in a deep dish with the baking powder, yeast and sugar; and stir well.
Mix the milk, oil and water together and add them to the previous mixture.
Mix well until blended paste is formed.
Cover the mixture and let it ferment for one hour.
In a large skillet let the oil boil and knead the dough by hand or by a dedicated machine, put dough in the oil on low heat.
Keep moving dough until it becomes golden.
Add a spoonful of honey as desired.
hints: Total Serving: Equal to 4 peices.

title: Pumpkin Soup
steps: In a preheated pot add olive oil then add the finely chopped onion.
Sauté for about 2 minutes, stirring often, until slightly softened but still vibrant.
Now, add the whole chicken breast and stir for 5 minutes on medium low heat, then add the spices.
Add the pumpkin, carrots, and zucchini (better to boil all beforehand to eliminate some K+)
Cook for about 30 minutes on medium heat.
Grind the soup with hand blinder until smoothing. (Add water for more smother texture)
Serve in a bowl and garnish with coriander.
Enjoy it with a squeeze of limon.

title: Chicken Fajita
ingredients: 4 bell peppers (medium size - Green, yellow, orange, and red – sliced)
steps: In a preheated pan add olive oil then add the onion, followed with the sliced bell paper.
Sauté for about 5 minutes, stirring often, until slightly softened but still vibrant.
Now, add the chicken breast and stir for 5 minutes on medium low heat.
Add the spices gradually and stir for more 5 minutes on medium low heat.
Set aside.
Bring your Tortilla bread and start filling with lettuce (optional)
Stuff you sandwich with the Fajita, Add a squeeze of lemon (optional)
In the same pan, add some olive oil and roast your sandwich (3 minutes each side)

title: Fatosh Salad
steps: Cut the cucumber, onion, pepper, tomato and radish into medium pieces.
Add the salt, olive oil and lemon and stir well, then add the pomegranate molasses.
Cut the bread and roast it in the oven at 180° C for 5 minutes until it becomes brown and place it over the salad. Place in a serving dish.
hints: Serving is for 1

title: Caesar Salad with Chicken
steps: Place a little olive oil in a hot skillet and add the chicken. Cook the chicken and then cut in the form of long fingers.
In a deep dish cut the lettuce into medium-sized pieces.
Mix the garlic with salt and vinegar until well blended.
Put the mixture over the lettuce.
Add chicken and cheese on top.
hints: Portions: 1 Serving Size: 1 salad

title: Baked macaroni cheese
description: Using butternut squash to make a creamy sauce, this delicious adaption of a family favourite is low salt, low potassium, low phosphate, and low protein.
steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C / 140°C fan / gas mark 3. Halve and deseed the butternut squash. Place flesh side down in a roasting tin and pour in 200ml water. Bake in the oven for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Allow the squash to cool slightly before scooping out the flesh with a spoon. Add to a blender with the coconut milk to make a smooth puree.

Once pureed, heat gently in a saucepan. Add Dijon mustard, cider vinegar and crumble in stock cube. Season with pepper and add a little water to the sauce if needed. Simmer for 20 minutes until it thickens.
Bring a large pan of water to boil. Add the macaroni and cook for 7 minutes. It will continue to cook as it bakes. Drain the pasta and combine with the sauce, pouring them in to an oven-proof dish.
Grate the cheese and combine with the breadcrumbs, almonds and finely chopped parsley if using. Sprinkle over the pasta and bake in the oven for 10 minutes until golden brown.
Bring a saucepan of water to the boil and add the broccoli. Cook until tender, drain and serve with the pasta.
hints: Chef's note
A twist on a classic, this version of macaroni and cheese is a lovely comforting meal that can be frozen for batch cooking.
Carbohydrate
The pasta and breadcrumbs are the main source of carbohydrate in this dish and the value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate
In this dish, butternut squash is used for the sauce which adds a healthy twist and keeps the recipe low in potassium.
Potassium/phosphate
This dish is low in phosphate, although it does contain some phosphate, from the cheese. If you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, ensure you take it with this dish.
Protein
This dish is low in protein and suitable if you are following a low protein diet.
Gluten free
Use gluten-free pasta, breadcrumbs and stock.
Healthier option
To increase the fibre in this dish, try using a wholemeal pasta in place of the macaroni pasta.
Cheaper option
This is a relatively inexpensive dish. To save money you could make your own breadcrumbs.
Storage

Once cooled, store in an airtight container and keep in the fridge. Use within 3 days and reheat thoroughly before serving. If freezing, portion at the end of step 4 in an airtight container. Defrost thoroughly, then add the topping mix and continue to cook from step 5.
Tips
To make fresh breadcrumbs, tear the bread into pieces and drop it into a food processor fitted with a blade. Whiz the bread in bursts until you have breadcrumbs of the size you want.
Tips
For a shortcut you could buy pre-packaged fresh chopped butternut squash or frozen squash and cook according to the packet instructions before continuing with step 2.

title: Chicken fajitas
description: This healthy recipes contains a moderate amount of calories and good source of protein.
ingredients: 400g tinned black beans, drained and rinsed
160g guacamole (or you can make this yourself, see tips section)
steps: Make the fajita seasoning by mixing all the ingredients together. Add the chicken strips and olive oil and mix until all combined.

Preheat the air fryer to 190°C in roasting setting. Mix the vegetables and beans in with the chicken and cook for 15 minutes, shaking the basket twice during cooking. This recipe can also be cooked in a frying pan on the hob if preferred. Pan-fry the chicken in the olive oil until browned all over, then add the rest of ingredients and cook over a medium heat for 15 minutes.
Make the salad dressing by adding all the ingredients to a bowl and whisk together. Add this dressing to the diced cucumber, salad leaves and tomatoes just before serving and combine well.
Once the chicken fajita mixture is cooked serve it with tortillas, soured cream and guacamole. Serve with the prepared salad on the side.
hints: Chef's note
This quick and easy recipe is perfect for a mid-week supper.
Portion size guidance for children

Young child (age 5-9): ½ adult portion
Portion size guidance for children
Older child (age 10-13): ¾ adult portion

Teenagers (14+): 1 adult portion
Portion size guidance for children

Some children do have bigger appetites than others. You child’s portion may need to be changed to fit their typical diet if you think the recommended serving sizes are too large or small. We would advise speaking with your dietitian prior to increasing the serving size if your child has struggled to manage potassium or phosphate.
Carbohydrate
The tortillas are the main source of carbohydrate in this recipe, and the value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate

Despite the use of some high potassium ingredients, such as Avocado, this recipe is low in potassium, when following the quantities in the ingredients, the cooking method, and the serving sizes. Therefore, suitable for those advised to lower potassium in their diet. This recipe is also low in phosphate, however it does contain some phosphate, mainly provided by the chicken, tortilla wraps and cheese, therefore if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder you should take as directed.
Potassium/phosphate

To lower the phosphate further you could consider replacing some or all of the meat with a plant-based alternative, such as 250g timed black beans-drained. However, this will also reduce the protein content of the recipe.
Protein
This recipe provides a source of protein. If you have been advised to eat less protein, consider reducing chicken to 100g and increasing beans to 200g-250g.
Energy

If you need to gain weight, have a growing child who needs more calories, or have a poor appetite, you can use a tablespoon of extra oil to cook the chicken. Adding extra meat or cheese to increase calories will increase phosphate content of the recipe.
Vegetarian
Consider using 200g tempeh or tofu instead of chicken.
Vegan
Consider using non-dairy sour cream alternatives.
Gluten free
Use gluten-free tortillas.
Healthier option
Use wholemeal tortilla wraps.
Cheaper option
Use vegetable/sunflower oil.
Cheaper option
Use a vinegar that you have in the kitchen.
Cheaper option
If you don’t have all the spices handy, consider using fajita seasoning mix (check for no added salt versions).
Cheaper option
Use Iceberg lettuce instead of mixed salad leaves.
Cheaper option
Use any smooth mustard of your choice.
Storage
This dish is best eaten freshly made. Any leftover dressing can be stored in the fridge for up to a week.
Tips
This can be served with Taco shells or rice as an alternative.

title: Broccoli and cauliflower pasta bake
description: For a speedy meal, this recipe can be prepared earlier in the day and cooked in the oven later (ensure it is refrigerated in the meantime).
steps: Preheat oven to 165°C. Bring a pan of water to the boil and add the pasta, cook for 5 minutes. Add the broccoli and cauliflower into the pan and cook for a further 8 minutes or until all cooked, then drain.
Mix the black pepper and dried herbs into the cream cheese in a bowl.
Tip the pasta and vegetables into a baking dish and stir in the cream cheese mix. Sprinkle with breadcrumbs and cheddar cheese. Cook for 30 minutes until golden brown.
Remove from oven and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
hints: Chef's note
An indulgent, creamy dinner, this meal is high in energy but low in salt, phosphate and potassium.
Carbohydrate
The pasta is the main source of carbohydrate in this main meal. The value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate

This dish is low in potassium, because the quantities per person have been carefully measured. If you have been advised to follow a low potassium diet ensure you keep to the quantities stated. This recipe is low in phosphate, however does contain some phosphate, therefore, if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder ensure you take them with this dish.
Protein
Protein is provided by the cheddar and cream cheese. To reduce the protein, you could use vegan alternatives that are often lower in protein than dairy sources.
Storage
For a speedy meal, this recipe can be prepared earlier in the day and cooked in the oven later (ensure it is refrigerated in the meantime). Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2 days.

title: Chana chaat
description: This is a high protein, low potassium snack suitable for somebody on dialysis, but so tasty that everybody will want some.
steps: To prepare the vegetables, chop the tomato, onion and cucumber into small, similar-sized pieces and place in a bowl. Chop the chilli and set aside for later.
Drain the chickpeas and add to the tomato, onion and cucumber mixture. Stir.
Add the lemon juice and the chana chaat masala. Stir well to combine.
Divide the mixture between three dishes. Top with the yogurt and add chopped chilli to taste.
hints: Chef's note
Chana chaat is tangy, fresh and easy to make, with no cooking involved. This savoury version is kidney-friendly and has been designed for those who wish to eat something traditional during Ramadan.
Carbohydrate
The yogurt, chickpeas, tomatoes and cucumber are all sources of carbohydrate in this dish. The total carbohydrate value has been provided for those who are trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate

Raw vegetables are high in potassium but if you follow the serving sizes specified, this dish is low in potassium overall. Each serving contains two portions of fruit and vegetables so please be mindful if you have more through the rest of the day.
Potassium/phosphate
If you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, ensure you take them with this dish.
Protein
Chickpeas are a good source of protein, making this a high protein snack, which is ideal for those on dialysis.
Vegan
Use a dairy-free yogurt.
Healthier option
To reduce the fat content of this dish, you could serve it with a low-fat yogurt or without the yogurt.
Storage
The chana chaat can be stored in an airtight container and kept in the fridge for up to two days.

title: Cheddar and sage savoury scones
description: Higher in protein than some snacks, these scones could make a nice treat while on dialysis.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C/ 170°C fan/ gas mark 5. Line a baking tray. In a bowl, mix flour, cream of tartar and bicarbonate of soda, then rub in the butter until it looks like fine breadcrumbs.
Mix in 80g of the grated cheddar and the dried sage. Make a well in the centre and pour in the milk. Using a knife in a cutting motion, mix into a dough.

Sprinkle your work surface and hands with flour, turn out the dough and work until smooth, then form into a round shape about 3cm thick. Place onto the baking tray and mark into 8 wedges. Brush with a beaten egg and sprinkle with remaining 20g cheddar.
Cook for 20 minutes until golden. Best served warm with a little butter.
hints: Chef's note
A tasty savoury alternative to a bread roll with soup, or enjoy in your packed lunch.
Carbohydrate
The main source of carbohydrate is the flour in these scones, carbohydrate values have been included for those trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate
Cream of tartar is a source of potassium but lower in phosphate than baking powder. The amount used allows this recipe to be used as an occasional snack on a low potassium diet.
Potassium/phosphate
Organic soya milk is lower in phosphate and potassium than cow's milk so is used here to reduce the phosphate and potassium content.
Potassium/phosphate
Cheese and baked goods are often high in phosphate so please take a phosphate binder with this snack if you are prescribed one.
Protein
The scone ingredients (milk, egg and cheddar) mean that they wouldn’t be suitable for somebody following a low protein diet.
Gluten free
Use gluten-free flour.
Healthier option
Use wholemeal flour and reduced fat cheese.
Storage
Will keep in an airtight tub in the fridge for three days.

title: Butternut squash and goat’s cheese parcels
description: Boiling the vegetables in this dish helps to lower the potassium, but by adding the goat’s cheese there is still plenty of flavour.
ingredients: 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
A pinch of ground black pepper
steps: Preheat oven to 180°c/ 160°c fan/ gas mark 4. Put the sweet potato and butternut squash into a saucepan, cover with water and bring to boil, cook until soft.

Drain the sweet potato and butternut squash and tip them into a roasting tray with the chopped onion. Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with black pepper and bake for 20 minutes. Remove from oven and cool.

Cut the pastry into 8 equal rectangles. Place 4 rectangles onto a lined baking tray and spoon ¼ of the vegetable mix into middle of each rectangle, leaving a gap all the way around edge. Top each vegetable mixture with 15g crumbled goat’s cheese. Brush a little of the beaten egg onto the pastry edge all the way around.

Take your 4 remaining rectangles, loosely fold in half lengthways and cut 5 slits through both layers, leaving a border. Unfold and lay over the 4 parcels, pressing the edges down onto the egg-washed edges of the bottom layer to seal your parcel.
Brush the top with egg-wash and sprinkle with sesame seeds or onion seeds and cook for 25 minutes until golden. Once cooked, remove from oven.
Once cooked, remove from the oven, and serve with the green salad.
hints: Chef's note
A delicious dish that’s quick and easy to prepare.
Carbohydrate
The main sources of carbohydrate in this meal are the sweet potato, butternut squash and pastry. Carbohydrate values have been provided for those trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate
We have boiled the butternut squash and sweet potato rather than baking to reduce the potassium content.
Potassium/phosphate
There is only a small amount of soft cheese in this dish to provide phosphate and therefore the overall phosphate content is low.
Protein
This dish is low in protein; you could consider doubling the cheese in order to increase the protein but maintain a low potassium and phosphate meal.
Gluten free
Use gluten-free pastry.
Vegan
Use vegan cheese.
Healthier option
Pastry is high in fat; for a healthier option you could omit the top layer of pastry and have an open parcel.
Tips
Butternut squash and sweet potato are available pre-prepared in the freezer section of most supermarkets if you find them difficult to peel at home.

title: Chicken Caesar wraps
description: A delicious high protein wrap, that is kidney and lunchbox friendly. It’s also low in potassium and phosphate, so is ideal to take to dialysis.
steps: Shred the cooked chicken into strips and add to a bowl with the chopped lettuce leaves and crushed garlic.
Shave thin slices of the parmesan into the bowl, then add the mayonnaise and Worcestershire sauce and stir gently to combine, seasoning with pepper.
To assemble the wraps, spoon ¼ of the mixture onto the bottom half of a tortilla. Fold the bottom of the tortilla up and over the filling.
Make two folds on either side and roll it up tightly. Repeat with the remaining three tortillas. Eat whole or cut in half to serve immediately, or wrap in foil to keep whole until you want to eat it.
hints: Chef's note
The classic Caesar salad has been reworked into a wrap, which makes the perfect quick lunch or light dinner.
Carbohydrate
The main source of carbohydrate in this dish comes from the tortilla wrap. The carbohydrate value of this dish has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate

If you stick to the serving sizes provided in this recipe, this dish is low in both potassium and phosphate. Both the chicken and Parmesan cheese contain phosphate, but the small portion used in this recipe keeps the overall phosphate content low. If you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, ensure you take them with this dish.
Protein
The chicken and cheese used in this recipe provide a source of protein which is great for people receiving dialysis and anyone who needs to eat more protein.
Gluten free
Use gluten-free tortilla wraps.
Vegetarian
Use meat-free chicken-style pieces or chickpeas instead. Check that your Parmesan cheese is suitable for vegetarians.
Vegan
Use meat-free chicken-style pieces or chickpeas instead. Use a suitable dairy-free mayonnaise and dairy-free hard Italian-style cheese.
Healthier option

There is no added salt in this recipe. The Parmesan cheese, Worcestershire sauce, mayonnaise, and tortilla wraps do contain salt, which makes this recipe slightly above the range to be classified as a low salt dish. To minimize the salt content, choose wraps with the lowest salt content. Measure the Worcestershire sauce, mayonnaise, and Parmesan cheese to avoid adding too much. To lower the salt content even further, you could consider using a teaspoon of lemon juice to replace the Worcestershire sauce and some natural yoghurt in place of the mayonnaise.
Healthier option
If you would like to lower the fat in this dish, choose a light mayonnaise.
Healthier option
Using a wholemeal wrap will increase the fibre in your diet.
Storage
Once made, keep in the fridge and use within two days. When packing for lunch, we recommend using a cool pack to keep it chilled.
Tips
If you don’t need four portions, you can scale the recipe down.

title: Bean and couscous salad
description: A low protein dish that is easy to prepare. It makes a great lunch time meal and is low in potassium, phosphate and salt.
ingredients: 400g tin three bean salad, in water
steps: Chop the onion and pepper and set aside.
Make the vegetable stock and measure the couscous. Stir the hot vegetable stock into the couscous, cover and leave to sit for five minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a small pan. Sauté the onion on a low heat for five minutes or until soft, then remove the pan from the heat.

Uncover the couscous and use a fork to fluff it up. Add the cooked onion and fresh pepper, then drain the bean salad and add to the couscous. Stir gently until well mixed. If using parsley, sprinkle it over the salad before serving.
hints: Chef's note
An easy vegan bean and couscous salad that can be prepared in advance for a healthy lunch.
Carbohydrate
The main sources of carbohydrate in this dish come from the couscous and beans. The carbohydrate value of this dish has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate
Beans do contain potassium and phosphate, but when using the amount in this recipe, the overall levels are low. If you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, ensure you take them with this dish.
Protein

This recipe is low in protein which is great for people who have been advised to reduce their protein. If you have been advised to increase your protein, you may wish to add a small tin of tuna. Look for tuna in spring water and drain before use.
Gluten free
Use buckwheat or quinoa and a gluten-free vegetable stock for a gluten-free option.
Storage
This dish keeps well and can be stored in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Caribbean peppered prawns with coconut rice
ingredients: 1 bunch spring onions (white and green), finely diced
steps: Prepare the rice by putting the coconut milk and coconut oil into a pan and bring to the boil. Add the rice, bring back to the boil, then turn heat down to low and put a lid on pan. Cook the rice until all the liquid has been absorbed. Take off the heat and leave to rest for a few minutes.

While the rice is cooking, combine the prawns with the cornflour, black pepper, paprika and chilli flakes. Heat half the oil in a pan over a medium heat and fry the prawns – just briefly to re-heat if using cooked prawns; for longer if using raw prawns, to ensure they are cooked through.

In a separate pan, heat the remaining oil over a medium/low heat and cook the chillies, spring onions (white only) and garlic for about 3 minutes. Add in the cooked prawns, along with the green parts of the spring onions and toss everything together. The prawns have already been cooked so this is a quick toss together.
Prepare the side salad by combining the lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes and pepper and season with your favourite salad dressing.
Serve the prawns on top of the coconut rice, with a sprinkle of fresh coriander and salad on the side.
hints: Chef's note
A quick and easy prawn dish that’s low in phosphate, potassium and salt.
Carbohydrate
Rice is the main source of carbohydrate, and the value has been provided for those trained in insulin adjustment.
Phosphate/potassium

This recipe is low in potassium, when following quantities and serving sizes given, so is suitable if you have been advised to reduce the amount of potassium in your diet. It is also low in phosphate, but does contain some, mainly provided by the prawns, so if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, take as directed.
Protein
This recipe provides a source of protein. If you are advised to eat more protein, consider having extra protein in other meals of the day.
Food safety
If you are using raw prawns, make sure they are fully cooked to avoid infection risk.
Serving suggestion
This dish is best eaten freshly made.
Healthier option
If you would like to make this dish lower in fat, consider using light/reduced-fat coconut milk.

title: Asian sticky chicken salad
ingredients: 3 spring onions, finely sliced into lengths
¼ cucumber, cut into fine batons
40g of chopped of plain, unsalted almonds or peanuts, roughly chopped
steps: Lay the chicken breast between some cling film and pound with a rolling pin until flattened out. Slice the chicken into strips.
Mix the soy sauce, honey, garlic and half the sesame oil into a bowl and whisk to combine. Put the chicken into the marinade, mix well, cover and chill for at least 20 minutes.
Heat the remaining sesame oil in a frying pan over a medium/high heat, then add the chicken strips and fry until completely cooked through. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside on a plate.
Reduce heat and add the remaining marinade mix and cook until a sticky dressing is made, about 5 minutes. Allow to cool.
Boil a kettle full of water and pour boiling water into a bowl. Put the noodles into the water and leave for 3 minutes. Drain.
Tip the remaining ingredients into a bowl and gently incorporate the chicken and noodles. Serve with dressing drizzled over the top.
hints: Chef's note
A flavourful Asian-inspired salad, low in salt, potassium and phosphate.
Carbohydrate
The rice noodles are the main source of carbohydrate in this recipe, and the value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate

This recipe is low in potassium, when following the quantities in the ingredients and serving sizes. It is therefore suitable for those advised to reduce potassium in their diet. This recipe is also low in phosphate, however, it does contain some phosphate (mainly provided by the chicken and nuts) so if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, take as directed.
Protein
This recipe provides a source of protein. For a lower protein option, consider reducing the chicken to 75g and adding a small tin (200g) of drained chickpeas at step 6.
Tips
Sesame oil is more expensive, but worth the extra cost, as a small amount adds wonderful flavour. Reduced-salt soy sauce still contains salt, so measure carefully.

title: Cherry filo pastry tarts
description: A perfect pudding, suitable for everyone.
steps: Add frozen cherries, sugar and vanilla essence to a saucepan. Cook on medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring frequently. Gently break apart the cherries with a spatula. Mix together the arrowroot powder and water to form a paste.

Add the paste to the cooked cherries, stirring as you pour it in. Bring it to the boil, then remove from the heat and allow to cool. Preheat oven to 190°C / 170°C fan / gas mark 5 and grease a muffin tin.

Take three pastry sheets and cut each into four squares. Melt the butter and brush the pastry on each side and line six holes with two squares in each. Add one tablespoon of cherry filling to each. Fold the filo pastry edges over the top of the cherry filling to loosely close.

Brush each tart with additional butter. Bake in the oven for 10-15 minutes, until the pastry looks light golden brown all over. Remove from the oven and transfer to a cooling rack. Once cooled, dust with powdered sugar. Serve warm or at room temperature.
hints: Chef's note
Using frozen cherries and ready-made pastry means these tarts can be made for special occasions all year round.
Carbohydrate
The main source of carbohydrates in this dish are the cherries, sugars and filo pastry. The carbohydrate value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate
This recipe contains cherries which are high in potassium but when used in the amount specified in the recipe it remains a low potassium dish.
Potassium/phosphate
This dish contains a small amount of phosphate which mainly comes from the filo pastry. If you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, ensure you take them with this dish.
Protein
This dish is low in protein and makes a suitable pudding for a special occasion if you have been advised to follow a low protein diet.
Gluten free
It is sometimes difficult to find gluten-free ready-made filo pastry, therefore you may wish to use gluten-free puff pastry instead.
Vegan
Many ready-made filo pastry is dairy free. Use a dairy-free spread instead of butter.
Healthier option
If you want to reduce the amount of sugar or fat you eat, reduce the quantity of sugar used in the cherry filling, or replace with sweetener. Consider using a low-fat spread instead of the butter.
Cheaper option
Vanilla extract could be used instead of the vanilla pods.
Storage
Once cooled, store in an airtight container in the fridge and eat within two days.

title: Baked eggs and vegetables
ingredients: ½ teaspoon dried mixed herbs or chilli flakes
250g mixed frozen vegetables, defrosted and drained
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Oil a small oven-proof frying pan or small baking dish. Whisk some black pepper and the mixed herbs or chilli flakes into the eggs. Pour the eggs into the pan.
Pour the vegetables into the egg mixture and stir in.
Scatter the cheese over the top and bake for 12-15 minutes or until lightly golden.
Remove from the oven and let it sit on side for a few minutes. Toast the bread and spread with butter, serve.
hints: Chef's note
This low potassium and low phosphate frittata dish is simple and quick.
Carbohydrate
The bread is the main source of carbohydrate in this recipe, and the value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate

This recipe is low in potassium, therefore suitable for those advised to follow a low potassium diet. This recipe is also low in phosphate, however it does contain some phosphate, mainly provided by the eggs and cheese, therefore if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder you should take as directed.
Protein
This recipe is high in protein, therefore suitable for those advised to eat more protein, such as those receiving dialysis.
Healthier option

Although salt has not been added, this recipe is not low in salt. This is because the bread and cheese contain salt – you may want to check the amount of salt in your bread and choose one with the lowest salt

title: Celebration cake
ingredients: Sprinkles, colouring and decorations as desired
steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C /150°C fan / gas mark 3. Prepare your baking tray/tins: for a tray bake, grease and line (greaseproof paper) a 20cm x 30cm tin; for a round layered cake, grease and flour 2 x 17.5cm diameter cake tins; for cupcakes, line a muffin tin with cases.
Beat the butter and sugar together until pale and fluffy. Add in the flour, eggs, bicarb, cream of tartar, milk and vanilla, beating again until smooth.

Put mixture into appropriate tray/ tins /cases. Cooking times as follows: Tray bake: 40–45 minutes; Cakes: 23–25 minutes; Cup cakes: 18–20 minutes Bake all options until a skewer comes out clean. Remove from oven and cool in tray/cake tins/cases.

Make the icing. Beat the butter until soft, then beat in icing sugar. If you want to add colour or flavour, do so now. You can either spread the icing using a knife, or put into a piping bag and pipe on the decoration. For the cake, use some of the butter icing in the middle, then sandwich both cakes together and pipe remaining buttercream on the top. Add your chosen decorations.
hints: Chef's note
This versatile, kidney-friendly recipe can be made as a cake, cupcakes or traybake and is perfect for birthdays or other celebrations.
Portion guidance for children
Serving sizes are based on adult portions.
Portion guidance for children
This celebration cake recipe makes 12 adult portions.
Portion guidance for children
Here is a guide for children:
Portion guidance for children
Toddler (age 1-4): ¼ portion
Portion guidance for children
Young child (age 5-9): ½
Portion guidance for children
Older child (age 10-13): ¾
Portion guidance for children
Teenagers (14+): 1
Portion guidance for children

Some children do have bigger appetites than others. You child’s portion may need to be changed to fit their typical diet if you think the recommended serving sizes are too large or small. We would advise speaking with your dietitian prior to increasing the serving size if your child has struggled to manage potassium or phosphate.
Carbohydrate
Flour and sugar are the main source of carbohydrate, and the value has been provided for those trained in insulin adjustment.
Phosphate/potassium

This recipe is low in potassium, when following ingredient quantities and serving sizes. It is also low in phosphate, but does contain some, mainly from the flour, so if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, take it as directed.
Healthier option
This is a high-energy recipe to be enjoyed occasionally as part of a balanced diet. Serve with berries, or another fruit, to help boost its nutritional value.
Gluten free
Use gluten-free flour.
Storage
Once cooled, keep in an airtight container for 5 days.
Tips

This is a versatile recipe you can adapt for different occasions – dress it up or dress it down! It’s low in salt, potassium and phosphate, making it a delicious treat for everyone to enjoy as an occasional treat. By using low-phosphate raising agents, like bicarbonate of soda and cream of tartar, it helps to keep the cakes/cupcakes low in phosphate and kidney-friendly.

title: Asparagus and apple egg-fried rice
description: A very quick vegetarian dish, low in salt, protein, potassium and phosphate.
ingredients: 1 inch piece of ginger, finely chopped
3 spring onions, sliced (separating the white and green parts)
220g asparagus, chopped (separating the stalks and tips)
1 small handful fresh coriander, roughly chopped
steps: Prepare all the ingredients, then cook the rice as per the package instructions, however avoid overcooking – you still want a slight bite to the rice. Once ready, drain and set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large frying pan or wok over a medium heat. Once hot, add the eggs and gently scramble with some black pepper. Set aside in a bowl once cooked.
Heat the frying pan or wok with the remaining oil. Add the garlic and ginger and cook over high heat, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant and lightly browned.

Add the red onion, whites of the spring onion and tomatoes. Cook, stirring, for 5 minutes. Add the asparagus stalks and cook, stirring, for 1 minute. Then add the asparagus tips and apple, cooking for another 1-2 minutes.
Add the rice in clumps and then use wooden spoons or spatulas to stir, toss and break up the rice. Fry, constantly stirring, for 3 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, cooked eggs, chopped green parts of the spring onions, and chopped coriander. Toss. Then add the sesame oil, toss, and add sliced chilli pepper, if using. Serve.
hints: Chef's note
An all-veggie egg fried rice with a tango of asparagus and apple.
Carbohydrate
The rice is the main source of carbohydrate in this recipe, and the value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate

Despite the use of some high potassium ingredients, such as asparagus and tomatoes, this recipe is very low in potassium, when following the quantities in the ingredients, and the serving sizes. Therefore, suitable for those advised to lower potassium in their diet.
Potassium/phosphate
This recipe is also low in phosphate, however it does contain some phosphate, mainly provided by the egg, therefore if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder you should take as directed.
Protein
This recipe is low in protein, therefore suitable for those advised to eat less protein. If you have been advised to eat more protein, then you could add 200-300g of cooked cod.
Cheaper option
Use long-grain rice instead of jasmine rice.
Gluten free
Use a gluten-free soy sauce.
Healthier option
Use brown instead of white rice to provide more fibre.
Storage
This dish is best eaten freshly made.

title: Braised tofu with mushrooms
description: This meal is low in potassium and phosphate but a good source of meat-free protein for somebody who is on dialysis.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon oyster sauce (use a vegetarian version to make this dish vegetarian/vegan)
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions. Parboil the carrots and pak choi for 5-10 minutes and drain the water afterwards.
Separate the oyster mushrooms from the cluster and slice the king oyster mushrooms.

Fry the tofu in a pan with one tablespoon of oil until golden on both sides. Cook in batches until all the tofu is cooked (approximately 5 minutes each side). Move the tofu onto a clean plate with kitchen towel on it to absorb the excess oil.
Add the garlic (if using), carrots, both types of mushrooms and pak choi into the heated pan with the other tablespoon of oil. Stir-fry them until they soften.
Put the cooked tofu back into the pan. Add the oyster sauce, soy sauce and sugar. Stir gently.
Mix the cornflour with one teaspoon of cold water. Slowly pour in the fluid and stir gently at the same time. Cook until the sauce is thickened and then serve with the rice.
hints: Chef's note
A classic, Hong Kong style meat-free dish. Rich, hearty and warming. Suitable for everyone in the family.
Carbohydrate
The rice is the main source of carbohydrate in this recipe, and the value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate

This recipe is low in potassium, despite the use of mushrooms, a high potassium vegetable. This is because the quantities have been kept to a minimum, therefore please ensure you follow the quantities for all the ingredients and the serving sizes.
Potassium/phosphate
This recipe is also low in phosphate, however it still contains phosphate, provided by the tofu and rice, therefore, if you are prescribed a phosphate binder you should take as directed.
Protein
This recipe is high in protein, which makes it suitable for those advised to eat more protein.
Gluten free
Use a gluten-free soy sauce such or Tamari and a gluten-free oyster sauce.
Vegetarian / Vegan
Replace the oyster sauce with a vegetarian version.
Healthier option

To increase the fibre of this dish consider using a wholegrain brown rice in place of a white rice. Be mindful that the low-salt soy sauce and oyster sauce are both high salt ingredients, therefore you should measure these carefully to avoid adding additional salt.
Storage
This dish is best eaten fresh.
Tips
To reduce cooking time, cut the tofu into 1cm cubes and cook using an extra tablespoon of oil.

title: Baked macaro-no-cheese
description: Using butternut squash for the creamy sauce, this delicious vegan dish is low salt, low potassium, low phosphate, and low protein, so it is suitable for everyone.
steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C / 140°C fan / gas mark 3. Halve and deseed the butternut squash. Place flesh side down in a roasting tin and pour in 200ml water. Bake in the oven for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Allow the squash to cool slightly before scooping out the flesh with a spoon. Add to a blender with the coconut milk to make a smooth puree.

Once pureed, heat gently in a saucepan. Add Dijon mustard, cider vinegar and crumble in stock cube. Season with pepper and add a little water to the sauce if needed. Simmer for 20 minutes until it thickens
Bring a large pan of water to boil. Add the macaroni and cook for 7 minutes. It will continue to cook as it bakes. Drain the pasta and combine with the sauce, pouring them in to an oven proof dish.
Combine the breadcrumbs, almonds, vegan cheese and parsley if using. Sprinkle over the pasta and bake in the oven for 10 minutes until golden brown.
Bring a saucepan of water to the boil and add the broccoli. Cook until tender, drain and serve with the pasta.
hints: Chef's note
A twist on a classic, this vegan version of macaroni and cheese is a lovely comforting meal that can be frozen for batch cooking.
Carbohydrate
The pasta and breadcrumbs are the main source of carbohydrate in this dish and the value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate

In most vegan cheese-based dishes, nutritional yeast is added to provide the cheesy flavour, however nutritional yeast is high in potassium. In this dish, butternut squash is used instead, which adds a healthy twist and keeps the overall recipe low in potassium.
Potassium/phosphate
This dish is low in phosphate, although it does contain some phosphate, therefore, If you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, ensure you take them with this dish.
Protein
This dish is low in protein and suitable if you are following a low protein diet.
Gluten free
Use gluten-free pasta, breadcrumbs and stock.
Healthier option
To increase the fibre in this dish, try using a wholemeal pasta in place of the macaroni pasta.
Cheaper option
This is a relatively inexpensive dish. However, you could try serving with broccoli if the purple sprouting broccoli is out of season or expensive. To save money you could make your own breadcrumbs.
Storage

Once cooled, store in an airtight container and keep in the fridge. Use within 3 days and reheat thoroughly before serving. If freezing, portion at the end of step 4 in an airtight container. Defrost thoroughly, then add the topping mix and continue to cook from step 5.
Tips
To make fresh breadcrumbs, tear the bread into pieces and drop it into a food processor fitted with a blade. Whiz the bread in bursts until you have breadcrumbs of the size you want.
Tips
For a shortcut, you could buy pre-packaged fresh chopped butternut squash or frozen squash and cook according to the packet instructions before continuing with step 2.

title: Caribbean style cauliflower au gratin
description: A low potassium and a low-salt meal that is great for freezing as a ready to eat post-dialysis meal. Just add a crusty roll to complete the meal.
steps: Preheat the oven to to 170°C/ 140°C fan/ gas mark 3. Add the cauliflower florets to a pan of water and boil. Allow to boil for 3 minutes, then remove from the heat and drain.
In a separate pan, melt the butter. Remove from the heat and stir in the flour until smooth. Return to the heat and add the milk, whisking to combine and thicken. This will make a roux (white sauce).
Add the black pepper, onion and grated cheese to the white sauce. Stir to combine.
Place the drained cauliflower into an oven proof dish and slowly pour over your sauce.
Place the drained cauliflower into an oven proof dish and slowly pour over your sauce.
Divide into two portions and serve with a crusty bread roll as a complete main meal.
hints: Chef's note
A traditional side dish but served as a main meal with crusty bread to complete it.
Carbohydrate
The bread roll, flour and milk are the main source of carbohydrate in this dish and the values have been provided for those who have trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate

Although this meal does contain some potassium, overall, when keeping to the portion size suggested, this meal is low in potassium and can be enjoyed as part of a low potassium diet. Note, this is not a side dish but a complete meal.
Potassium/phosphate
This dish is high in phosphate, mainly due to the cheese and milk, therefore, if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder ensure you take them with this meal.
Potassium/phosphate
Note: if you are following a low phosphate diet, be sure to include the milk in this recipe as part of your allowance for the day.
Protein
This recipe is high in protein, provided by the cheese and milk. If you have been advised to reduce your protein, then consider replacing the cow’s milk with a rice, oat or almond milk.
Gluten free
Use a gluten-free flour and gluten-free bread rolls.
Storage
Once cooked, this dish can be kept in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheated. Can also be frozen before or after cooking in the oven.

title: Caribbean beef patties
description: A tasty, filling dish, accompanied with a delicious fresh salad. Overall, this recipe is low in salt, potassium and phosphate.
ingredients: 1 small onion (or ½ a medium onion), finely chopped
1 teaspoon of green seasoning or 1 very low salt stock cube
1 small tin of pineapple (drained and chopped)
½ red and ½ yellow peppers, cubed
1 small 200g tin of sweetcorn or 160g of frozen sweetcorn
steps: Heat a large, lidded frying pan over a medium heat; add the oil and fry the onion for 5 minutes, then add the crushed garlic and minced beef and cook until the mince is browned. Add one teaspoon of the turmeric, the tomato purée, green seasoning or stock cube and 200ml water, mix well to combine. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.

After 15 minutes of simmering with the lid on, remove the lid, stir through the chopped fresh coriander and let it simmer for another 5 minutes without a lid. Leave the mixture to cool while you prepare the pastry.

Preheat the oven to 200°C / 180°C fan / gas mark 7. On a floured surface, roll the shortcrust pastry block out to a thickness of 2mm. With a saucer or small plate/bowl to draw around, mark out 8 circles with a 15cm diameter.

Scoop the mince mixture from the pan and pile it onto one side of each of the pastry circles. Beat the egg. Brush the egg wash around the edge of the pastry circles and fold over and seal (push down with a fork to get a good seal). Put the patties on a lined baking tray and brush the tops with the egg wash. Bake for 20-30 minutes or until golden brown.
While the patties are baking, prepare the salad. In a large bowl, add the pineapple, sweetcorn, tomatoes, cucumber and peppers. Mix the vinegar, sugar and black pepper in a small jug and pour over.
Remove the patties from the oven when they are piping hot and the pastry is browned and crispy all over. Allow to cool for 5 minutes and then serve two patties per person, with the salad.
hints: Chef's note
These traditionally Caribbean beef patties make a great main meal when served with this colourful salad.
Carbohydrate
The pastry is the main source of carbohydrate in this recipe, and the value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate

Despite the use of some high potassium ingredients, such as tomatoes and tomato puree, this recipe is low in potassium, when following the quantities in the ingredients, and the serving sizes. Therefore, suitable for those advised to lower potassium in their diet.
Potassium/phosphate
This recipe is also low in phosphate, however it does contain some phosphate, mainly provided by the beef, therefore if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder you should take as directed.
Protein

This recipe is a source of protein, therefore suitable for those advised to eat more protein, such as those receiving dialysis. If you have been advised to eat less protein then you may wish to replace half of the beef with kidney beans or a different pulse (see the vegan and vegetarian options).
Gluten free
Use a gluten-free pastry.
Vegetarian
Replace beef with a 400g tin of kidney beans or another pulse (drained).
Vegan
Replace beef with a 400g tin of kidney beans or another pulse (drained).
Storage
Once the patties have cooked, cool and store in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Can be reheated or eaten cold.

title: Beetroot and goat's cheese quiche
description: An indulgent quiche that is low in salt but full of flavour.
ingredients: A pinch of ground black pepper
steps: To make the pastry: put the flour, onion seeds, parmesan and paprika in a bowl and combine. Add in the butter and rub in with your fingers until it resembles fine breadcrumbs.

Add the egg, mixing with a knife until it all starts to come together. Then use your hands to bring the mixture together into a ball of dough. Tip out on a floured surface and knead a little to smooth the dough. Wrap in cling film and set aside until ready to use.

To make the quiche: butter and flour a 23cm (9 inch) diameter flan ring. On a floured surface, roll the pastry out until large enough to line the flan ring. Gently lower the pastry into the tin and press it into the corners. Prick the bottom of the pastry with a fork.

Preheat the oven to 180°C / 160°C fan/ gas mark 4. Put the cubed beetroot and the crumbled goat’s cheese into the flan base. Whisk the eggs and double cream together in a jug, add in the pepper. Pour the mixture over the beetroot and goat’s cheese.
Sprinkle grated cheddar over the top of the quiche then bake in the oven for 25 minutes until nicely golden and the egg mixture has set. Leave to cool in the tin. Once cooled, turn out and serve.
Prepare the salad by combining the rocket, tomatoes and cucumber and then dress with the lemon or lime juice. Serve into six portions.
hints: Chef's note
A nice supper dish or for lovely for a special occasion. Leftover slices make great packed lunches.
Carbohydrate
The pastry is the main source of carbohydrate in this dish and the values have been provided for those who have trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate

Although this recipe does contain beetroot, tomatoes and other salad vegetables that are high in potassium, overall, when keeping to the portion sizes suggested, this dish is low in potassium and can be enjoyed as part of a low potassium diet.
Potassium/phosphate
Even though this dish is low in phosphate, it does contain some phosphate, provided by the cheese. Therefore, If you have been prescribed a phosphate binder ensure you take them with this dish.
Protein
This is a low protein dish, therefore suitable for those advised to reduce their protein intake.
Gluten free
The pastry can be made with gluten-free flour and a small teaspoon of Xanthan Gum.
Storage
This recipe will last in the fridge for three days. It can be served cold in packed lunches.
Tips
This recipe can also be made as individual quiches using a muffin tin. Just ensure the tin is well buttered and floured first and bake for a reduced time of 15 minutes.

title: Butternut squash and chickpea curry
description: A high fibre, filling vegetarian curry low in protein, potassium, phosphate and salt. Perfect for those reducing their protein.
steps: Peel, deseed and dice the butternut squash. Heat the oil in a large frying pan and cook the butternut squash for 2-3 minutes until lightly browned. Dice the onion and add to the pan, along with the curry paste and fry for another 3-4 minutes.

Pour over the stock, then cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the squash is tender. Drain and rinse the chickpeas then add with the tomatoes to the curry. Gently cook for 3-4 minutes, until the tomatoes slightly soften.
Bring saucepan of water to the boil. Rinse the rice and add to the boiling water. Cover and reduce the heat to a simmer for 20 minutes or until cooked.
Take the curry off the heat and stir through the yogurt and chopped coriander. Serve with the cooked rice and a wholemeal chapatti if you like.
hints: Chef's note
This quick and easy vegetable curry is a tasty midweek choice. Use a plant based yogurt or coconut cream for a vegan friendly meal.
Carbohydrate

The main source of carbohydrate in this dish comes from the rice and chapatis. The carbohydrate value of this dish has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment. If serving without chapatis you can increase the amount of rice from 40g to 60g uncooked rice per serving.
Potassium/phosphate

Although this dish contains some high potassium ingredients, such as the tinned tomatoes and the butternut squash, the amounts used in the recipe have been kept to a minimum to ensure the entire meal is still low in potassium and can therefore be enjoyed if following a potassium restriction.
Potassium/phosphate
Overall, this dish is low in phosphate, but if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder ensure you take them with this dish.
Protein

This dish is relatively low in protein per portion and is therefore suitable if you have been advised to follow a low protein diet. If you have been advised to follow a high protein diet you may wish to serve with 170g chicken if you eat meat. This can be diced and added at step 2.
Gluten free
When served with rice, this recipe is gluten-free.
Vegan
Use a plant-based yogurt or coconut cream.
Healthier option

The flavour of this dish comes from all the curry paste and herbs therefore additional salt is not required. The stock will contain some salt, but low or very low salt stock cubes or stockpots are readily available in supermarkets.
Cheaper option
This dish is relatively cheap. To make life easier, try using pre prepared or frozen butternut squash that is already peeled and diced!
Storage

If not eating all the curry immediately, separate before adding the yogurt. Allow to cool, place in an airtight container, refrigerate and consume within two days. Reheat and stir in the yogurt before serving. If freezing the curry, place in a sealed container in portions. Defrost and reheat thoroughly, stirring in the yogurt before serving. Rice should be served hot and eaten immediately after it is first cooked, do not keep and reheat. Serve with freshly-cooked rice.

title: Chicken and vegetable crumble
description: A wholesome meal with a small amount of parmesan and nuts to give some crunch without too much phosphate per portion. By boiling the vegetables first it keeps the potassium content low.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C / fan 170°C / gas mark 5 and bring a large saucepan of water to boil. Peel and dice the celeriac, sweet potatoes and carrots. Trim, clean and slice the leeks. Dice the chicken into equal size pieces.
Add the sweet potatoes and vegetables to the saucepan of boiling water. Boil for 10-15 minutes, drain and discard the water. Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and fry the chicken until cooked.
Add the drained vegetables to the chicken and add the vegetable stock. Simmer on a low heat for 5 minutes.
Stir together the crème fraîche with the flour and mustard. Stir into the chicken and vegetables until thickened, then add the sage. Remove from the heat.
For the crumble, use your fingertips to rub the butter, flour and ground almonds together until they resemble breadcrumbs. Grate and stir in the parmesan and add the flaked almonds.
Spoon the chicken and vegetable filling into an ovenproof dish and scatter the crumble on top. To cook, bake in the oven for 30-35 minutes until golden brown on top.
hints: Chef's note
This savoury crumble is delicious with a creamy chicken and vegetable filling and a crunchy, cheesy topping. Great for a family meal and suitable for home freezing.
Carbohydrate
The carbohydrate in this dish mainly comes from the sweet potato and the flour. The carbohydrate values have been provided for those trained in insulin adjustment.
Potassium/phosphate

Nuts are high in both phosphate and potassium but in the quantities used here almonds can still be included for a crunchy crumble topping. If you have been prescribed a phosphate binder ensure you take them with this dish. Boiling the vegetables and discarding the water helps to remove some of the potassium. Celeriac is often avoided due to its high potassium content but when boiled and used in the quantities provided it can be included on a low potassium diet.
Protein
